neither the risk difference nor the odds ratio reaches conventional statistical significance; the p-values suggest only marginal evidence
the hypothesis is concluded to be not supported

the null hypothesis of no effect cannot be ruled out at α=0.05
point estimates suggest a small positive association but uncertainty is too large for firm conclusions
the results are described as inconclusive and consistent with multiple scenarios
one possible scenario is that no true bias exists and referees do not discriminate by skin tone
another possible scenario is a small, undetectable bias (true effect 0.1-0.2pp) requiring a larger sample to detect
another possible scenario is that bias is heterogeneous, with effects cancelling out across leagues
another possible scenario is residual confounding from unmeasured playing-style or other factors
the 0.17pp point estimate represents roughly an 8% relative increase that could be socially meaningful despite lacking statistical significance
exploratory analyses revealed significant heterogeneity by league, with opposite patterns in different countries
the direction of the point estimate is consistent with implicit-bias hypotheses, but the evidence is weak
